extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, administrative tribunal designers, UIC administrators, and legal drafters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and proposed regulatory amendments governing appeals, adjudication, timing, access, organization, and remedial rules for unemployment insurance decisions and tribunals (Boards of referees, Umpire/Tribunal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedite pre-hearing procedure / minimize slowness
rubrics_metrics.description: The slowness of the pre-hearing process has a detrimental effect on public participation; expedite pre-hearing procedure to maintain the practical interest of litigants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance planning and structural changes (see Chapter 13) are required; reducing delays will incentivize appearance before the Umpire and improve participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal time limit to request hearing for all appellants
rubrics_metrics.description: All potential appellants and intervening parties, including the UIC, should be subject to the same time limit to request a hearing (proposed: fifteen days from docket filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose amending reg.185 so the fifteen-day period applies to all appellants and interveners; aligns with reg.184(5) period for filing representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of summons and proactive case planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribunals should actively use their authority to summon parties and third‑party witnesses and engage in better advance planning for hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forwarding files more quickly and allowing Umpires to devote time to case preparation will enable better decisions about summoning witnesses and parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of informality—minimize legal formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The informality embodied in sec.93(1) should be applied widely to encourage effective participation and avoid inhibiting the uninitiated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce legal formalities to the indispensable minimum because excessive formality tends to be detrimental to claimants' cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal aid policy—voluntary, independent, not automatic
rubrics_metrics.description: While expert representation increases claimants' chances, automatic universal legal aid for all claimants is unnecessary and may discourage responsible participation; avoid UIC-provided universal legal aid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage a variety of independent agencies, maintain tension/cooperation with UIC to preserve credibility; UIC should direct claimants to these agencies and may support sectoral conferences but should not itself provide blanket assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and cooperation with independent legal-aid agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC should direct appellants to independent agencies and support (including financially if needed) a technical conference to improve litigation practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference could bring together UIC, unions, specialized agencies, legal aid services, and tribunal members to produce materials useful for reform and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational objective: minimize internal delays
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative structures should be organized so as to minimize delays attributable to internal movements of files between units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two approaches discussed: computerization and integration/decentralization of functions; identify bottlenecks and take remedial action to shorten processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computerization design to reduce processing lags
rubrics_metrics.description: Computerization brings workload and manpower savings but may introduce time lags and transmission delays; systems should be designed/located to reduce these lags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decentralizing computer services (bringing computers closer to claimants/agents) appears to expedite processing by reducing geographic scope, reaction time, and transmission delays; design requires standardization to avoid imprecision blocking processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain separation between investigatory and adjudicative functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not fully integrate benefit control (investigation) with entitlement determination (adjudication) because the functions differ fundamentally and integration risks blurring roles and overloading staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial delegation (e.g., interview work to Agents II) may reduce referrals but could blur roles and overload Agents II; consider compensatory authority increases for Agents I and monitor experience to weigh advantages vs disadvantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid subordinating review tribunals to the administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Boards of referees should not be so incorporated into the UIC's organization that their independence and breadth of knowledge are compromised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current arrangements (premises, staffing, training provided by UIC) facilitate liaison but risk that referees acquire knowledge from only the UIC; reorganization proposals (Chapter 13) aim to remedy lack of independent attachment while preserving speed and simplicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable handling of retroactive decisions and overpayments
rubrics_metrics.description: Retroactive denial/withdrawal of benefits (sec.57) raises injustice where overpayments arise from UIC mistakes or technical failures; enforcement should distinguish fraud/bad faith from administrative error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empower UIC to write off benefits unduly paid where overpayment resulted from its own mistake or technical deficiency (except where claimant knew payments were not due); amend reg.175 and make write-off decisions appealable; limit absolute enforcement of sec.57 to conclusive evidence of bad faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid retroactivity where UIC's failure caused delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claimant's conduct was not deliberate and the UIC's failure to maintain contact delayed discovery, the UIC should avoid making disentitlement retroactive to force excessive repayment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy favors not applying retroactive repayment in these circumstances because it can be excessive relative to claimant's means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set and enforce strict deadlines for appeals at Board of referees level
rubrics_metrics.description: Three deadlines govern Board appeals: filing notice of appeal (sec.94: 30 days), writing the submission/summary, and the session/hearing of the Board (target: heard within 45 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose adding subsections to reg.179 requiring Commission to prepare and forward a summary within 14 days of appeal filing (with one 14-day extension available); failure by Commission to prepare/forward summary within periods => board deemed to have allowed the appeal; summary must be forwarded to chairman/members at least one week before hearing; Commission may correct account of facts until Board decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance standard for Board hearing times
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational standard: 90% of appeals should be heard within 30 days and the remainder within 45 days; include the 45-day standard in procedural provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce compliance by deeming appeals allowed if no decision is given within the prescribed period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chairman’s power to order joinder of similar appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid undue burden when many appeals arise from the same situation, the chairman should be empowered to order that several appeals with substantially the same issues be joined and heard together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed addition to reg.181 granting the chairman this power at any time after filing of notice of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct filing to Tribunal and Tribunal responsibility for case progression
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals should be made and filed at the office of the Tribunal (not with the administrative authority) so the Tribunal can solicit/receive parties' positions and ensure the procedure progresses normally to the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend reg.184 to require appeals to be filed at Tribunal, require Tribunal to send notice/copy to Commission and parties, and make Tribunal responsible for collecting observations of all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict deadlines for Commission to prepare and file appeal docket at Tribunal
rubrics_metrics.description: When Commission files or receives notice of an appeal, it must prepare a docket within 21 days containing: copy of appeal; all documents considered by Board; transcript of evidence (if any); written decision of Board; file the docket at the Tribunal office; and mail a copy to each interested party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission may file observations within 15 days of docket filing (or further time allowed by Tribunal); appellants/interested parties may file observations within 15 days of docket filing (or further time allowed). Tribunal decides questions of immediate interest and may render decision on documents filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for Tribunal/Umpire decisions with sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: Set a time limit of ninety (90) days for the Tribunal to reach a decision on an appeal; unless decision given within ninety days, it shall be deemed decided in favour of the claimant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose adding subsection to reg.186; similar sanction mechanism proposed at Board level (deemed allowance) to induce compliance with deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cap total litigation timeline (aggregate deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: With proposed time limits, the maximum length of litigation from initial Agent decision to Tribunal decision should be seven months (detailed day-by-day breakdown provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed schedule: initial decision (Day 0); appeal to Board +30; summary +14 (Day 44); Board hearing +45 (Day 75); appeal to Tribunal +45 (Day 120); filing representations +21 (Day 141); Tribunal decision +90 (Day 210).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to review—equalize rights of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Sec.95 improperly discriminates among claimants and employers; amend to give the same right of appeal to all potential appellants (UIC, claimants, employers, unions, employers' associations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain equality of all members of the public before government actions; consider whether equalization should be upward or downward—prefer requiring leave to appeal in certain unanimous Board decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave-to-appeal requirement and criteria when Board decision unanimous
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Board of referees decision is unanimous, right of appeal to the Tribunal should be contingent on prior recognition that 'there is a principle of importance involved in the case or that there are other special circumstances' justifying appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer requiring leave to appeal in such cases; criteria of importance and difficulty are already set down in the Act for claimants and employers (e.g., non‑unanimity, chairman finding important principle or special circumstances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribunal composition and operating procedures to ensure speed, impartiality, and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Review tribunals must be composed and operated so they render decisions quickly and impartially; decisions must be clear, logical, and legally sound to be authoritative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals cover access, organization of review tribunals, and decision quality; organization should balance independence with operational liaison while safeguarding impartiality and decision quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce formalities and ensure accessible hearing locations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ease of exercising the right of review depends on minimal formalities and the spatial/location choices for hearings; location should not create obstacles to access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design procedures and select hearing venues to minimize barriers to participation (travel/time/cost) and keep formal procedural requirements minimal.
